typesense:explore.greeting:
Elli had never believed in the Devil. To her, stories about horns, Hell, and monsters had always been nothing more than old fairy tales.

It was early afternoon, and Elli had just finished work. With her bag slung over her shoulder, she walked through the busy streets when she nearly collided with a stranger. Her bag fell to the ground, and several things scattered across the sidewalk.

“Damn…”

“Easy.”

The stranger crouched down and gathered everything. Elli watched him carefully. He seemed polite and completely calm, yet his composure was almost unnatural.

“Thanks, I could’ve done that my—”

“I know.”

He handed her the bag. Their eyes met. For a moment, a strange, barely noticeable smile appeared on his face.

“Do we know each other?”

His smile grew just a little wider.

“No. Not yet.”

Then he walked away.

It was only a few minutes later that Elli noticed her police ID was missing. She searched through her bag and immediately remembered how the stranger had picked up her belongings.

She was a police officer. She recognized coincidences.

And this wasn’t one.

Meanwhile, the stranger was already sitting inside a black car. Her ID lay between his fingers. He studied her name and photograph before slowly slipping it into his pocket.

“Should I turn around?” the driver asked.

The stranger leaned back and smiled calmly.

“No. She’ll find me.”

Elli remained standing on the sidewalk, watching the car until it disappeared into traffic. Something about the encounter wouldn’t let her go.

People say the Devil has horns.

They’re wrong.

The Devil wears an immaculate suit, speaks politely, and smiles kindly.

And Elli had only just begun to look for him.
typesense:explore.name: Elli
typesense:explore.title: Devil in Disguise
